page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.3xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine instance belonging to the high clock speed family. It is built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by a dedicated 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration allocates 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs via hyperthreading, backed by 35 MB of shared L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector extensions. System memory totals 24.0 GB RAM, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation tailored for CPU-intensive processing tasks.

Hardware resource provisioning reflects its compute focus, featuring no bundled local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs. All persistent storage must be attached via network-attached block volumes. Baseline network throughput is configured at 4 Gbps, and the server provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated network routing configurations.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier compute capabilities across synthetic and application workloads. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1281.0 and a multi-core score of 6420.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 13054.11. Code compilation tests yield a Clang benchmark score of 10550.0, while static web serving throughput reaches 10.1 GB/sec and in-memory Redis SET operations achieve 11.24 million operations per second. In machine learning inference, prompt processing for medium 7B models falls into the bottom quartile at 17.31 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of specialized tensor acceleration.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-efficient resource profile for compute-dense applications where paying for surplus RAM is unnecessary. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and moderate 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth serve as architectural constraints for I/O-intensive pipelines. The ecs.hfc6.3xlarge is well aligned for CI/CD compilation runners, batch computing, backend web services, and algorithmic processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.3xlarge is a high clock speed, compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring 6 physical cores and 12 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading, the instance provides 24.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio designed for compute-heavy workloads. It includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local ephemeral storage or GPU acceleration, and operates with a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle tier for CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6420.0 and 11.24 million Redis operations per second. Due to its balanced compute density without surplus RAM overhead, the ecs.hfc6.3xlarge is suited for software build pipelines, batch data processing, web serving, and general computation.
